PQC-MTC 1.0 API

Integrating a Different Database

The MTC services do not depend on SQLite, MySQL, JDBI, or a particular schema. To use PostgreSQL, Oracle, MongoDB, another SQL database, or a custom storage service, provide an adapter for the tree design selected by the application.

Choose the DAO interface for the tree design

Database integration interfaces and reference implementations
Tree design Interface to implement Reference implementations
Baseline MTC_Baseline_Data_Dao MTC_Data_Dao_SQLite
Append-only MTC_AppendOnly_Data_Dao MTC_Data_Dao_SQLite and MTC_Data_Dao_MySQL

Both specialized interfaces extend MTC_Data_Dao, which defines the shared certificate, node, and signed-state persistence operations. Implement the specialized interface directly; this also requires all inherited common operations.

Required operations

  • Common certificate operations: saveCerts, both getCert overloads, and getCertsByTimestamp.
  • Common node operations: saveNodes, loadNodes, getNodeByIndex, and getNodesByIndices.
  • Common state operations: saveStatement, getStatement, getLatestTimestamp, and getCertCounts.
  • Baseline-only operation: getNodeByCertInd, which selects the leaf for a certificate at a particular state timestamp.
  • Append-only operation: updateNodes, which expires the previous versions of dynamic nodes when the tree grows.

The append-only service does not call getCertsByTimestamp. An append-only adapter must still provide the method because it is inherited from the common interface; it may throw UnsupportedOperationException, as the supplied adapters do.

Behavioral and transaction requirements

  • getNodesByIndices must return one result for every requested index in the same order as the input list. Do not rely on the database's unordered IN query result.
  • getLatestTimestamp must return 0 when no state exists; single-record lookups should return null when no record exists, and collection lookups should return an empty list rather than null.
  • Persist hashes and signatures without changing their Base64 or PEM text, and keep all timestamps in milliseconds.
  • For a transactional database, the adapter should also implement DaoSupport. Every DAO call made by one build round must use the same transaction/connection so certificate inserts, node updates, node inserts, and the new signed state either all commit or all roll back. 
final class MyDatabaseDao
        implements MTC_AppendOnly_Data_Dao, DaoSupport, AutoCloseable {
    // Implement the inherited certificate, node, state, and transaction methods.
}

MyDatabaseDao dao = new MyDatabaseDao(/* connection settings */);
MTC_Service_AppendOnly service = new MTC_Service_AppendOnly(mldsa, dao);

dao.inTransaction(() -> {
    service.build(certificates, timestamp);
    return null;
});

JdbiTransactionSupport demonstrates how the SQLite and MySQL JDBI adapters bind all DAO calls in a build to one connection. A custom implementation may use its database driver's native transaction API instead. Queue consumption is not part of the generic MTC DAO: applications modeled on MTC_BuildRunner should consume their queue and call build inside the same transaction.

MTC Service (Baseline Design)

1. Initialize Cryptographic Engine & Admin Certificates

Initialize the MLDSA handler to generate the administrative key pair and self-issued root certificates.

MLDSA mldsa = new MLDSA();

// Prepare the Administrative DSA key pair
mldsa.AdminKGen();

// Generate and export the Admin's self-issued root certificate
X509Certificate selfIssuedCert = mldsa.genSelfIssuedAdCert();
String adminCertPem = mldsa.exportCertificate(selfIssuedCert, "ADMIN CERTIFICATE");

2. Issue User Certificates

Receive an ML-KEM public key (usually from a client device) and issue a standard X.509 digital certificate signed by the Admin.

// Generate a pair of ML-KEM keys for the user (Usually done client-side)
String[] kpair = mldsa.genKemKeys();
String kemPK = kpair[0];

String user_id = "U1";
int cert_ind = 0;
long valid_time = 24 * 3600 * 1000; // Validity: one day

// Generate and issue the user's digital certificate
X509Certificate userCert = mldsa.issueCertForUser(user_id, cert_ind, kemPK, System.currentTimeMillis(), valid_time);

// Export the certificate to standard PEM format
String userCertPemStr = mldsa.exportCertificate(userCert, "USER CERTIFICATE");

// Re-import and cryptographically verify the user's certificate locally
userCert = mldsa.importCertificate(userCertPemStr);
boolean isValid = mldsa.verifyCertInJava(userCert);

3. Initialize the MTC Service

Set up the local database DAO and initialize the MTC_Service.

// Initialize the database Data Access Object (DAO)
com.smu.example.baseline.MTC_Data_Dao_SQLite database = new com.smu.example.baseline.MTC_Data_Dao_SQLite(database_path);

// Initialize the Merkle Tree Component (MTC) Service
MTC_Service_Baseline mtc_Service = new MTC_Service_Baseline(mldsa, database);

// Temporarily reduce the standard duration for testing purposes (e.g., 10ms)
Utils.DURATION = 10;

4. Build MTC State

The MTC service maintains state over time. You can build an initial empty state, and append newly issued certificates over subsequent rounds.

4.1 Build Empty Initial State

long init_time = 100;
// Build the initial state tree without any certificates
mtc_Service.build(null, null, init_time);

// Retrieve and verify the generated state record
MTC_State_Record st = database.getStatement(init_time);

4.2 Append Certificates to State

rd = 3;
cert_num = 5;
pre_time = next_time;

// Calculate the next timestamp (simulating the passage of time)
next_time = pre_time + rd * Utils.DURATION;

// Generate new mock certificates to append to the state
long create_time = next_time;
long valid_time = 24 * 3600 * 1000; // Validity: one day
certs = gen_test_certs(cert_counter, cert_num, mldsa, create_time, valid_time);
cert_counter += cert_num;

// Build the MTC state incorporating the newly generated certificates
mtc_Service.build(certs, null,next_time);

5. Generate and Validate Membership Proof

Generate a cryptographic JSON proof for a specific user at a specific timestamp, and validate it locally.

// Generate a membership proof JSON for a specific user ID at a specific timestamp
String targetUserID = "UID-4";
String proof = mtc_Service.getMemberProof(targetUserID, p_time);

// Validate the cryptographic integrity and state of the generated proof
if (mtc_Service.validate(proof)) {
    log.info("Validation Passed: The user is a valid member at the specified time.");
} else {
    log.info("Validation Failed.");
}

MTC Service (Append-Only Design)

1. Initialize the MTC Service

Set up the local database DAO and initialize the MTC_Service.

// Initialize the database Data Access Object (DAO)
MTC_Data_Dao_SQLite database = new MTC_Data_Dao_SQLite(database_path);

// Initialize the Merkle Tree Component (MTC) Service
MTC_Service_AppendOnly mtc_Service = new MTC_Service_AppendOnly(mldsa, database);

// Temporarily reduce the standard duration for testing purposes (e.g., 10ms)
Utils.DURATION = 10;

2. Build MTC State

The MTC service maintains state over time. You can build an initial empty state, and append newly issued certificates over subsequent rounds.

2.1 Build Empty Initial State

long init_time = 100;
// Build the initial state tree without any certificates
mtc_Service.build(null, init_time);

// Retrieve and verify the generated state record
MTC_State_Record st = database.getStatement(init_time);

2.2 Append Certificates to State

rd = 3;
cert_num = 5;
pre_time = next_time;

// Calculate the next timestamp (simulating the passage of time)
next_time = pre_time + rd * Utils.DURATION;

// Generate new mock certificates to append to the state
long create_time = next_time; // Certificates are created at the next timestamp
long valid_time = 24 * 3600 * 1000; // Validity: one day
certs = gen_test_certs(cert_counter, cert_num, mldsa, create_time, valid_time);
cert_counter += cert_num;

// Build the MTC state incorporating the newly generated certificates
mtc_Service.build(certs, next_time);
